site.description: Local-first tennis tools from AceCrush: AceCrush Craft for grip size, racket profiles and stringing data on Android, syncing through your own Supabase account with no central AceCrush server, plus Swing Analysis for automatic swing segmentation on the desktop.

brandHero.headline:
Tennis tech that
runs on your device.
brandHero.subtext: AceCrush builds focused tools for players and coaches. Measurement runs on-device. Your records sync through your own Supabase account with row-level scoping, with no central AceCrush server: every user keeps their own data.
brandHero.craftCardBody: Measure your grip size from a palm photo, keep a profile for every racket, log each restring with expiry reminders, and convert tension across DT, RT, lbs and kg.
brandHero.swingCardBody: Drop in a match video and get every swing cut into its own clip, each labelled with ready, windup, contact and follow-through phases plus exact timecodes.

intro.headline:
Perfect Photo,
Perfect Grip
intro.subtext: On-device AI measures hand size via an A4 reference, recommends your optimal grip, and tracks your next string job.

howItWorks.heading: From photo to recommendation in under 30 seconds.
howItWorks.step1Body: Lay an A4 sheet flat on the table with your palm resting on it.
howItWorks.step2Body: Line the edges of the A4 sheet up with the green frame on screen, keep your palm open, fingers and heel fully in frame.
howItWorks.step3Body: AI returns the recommended size and adjacent sizes. You can fine-tune manually.

features.heading: What it does for you.
features.subheading: Five tools. One download. Works fully offline.
features.item1Body: On-device MediaPipe inference maps your palm to Yonex, Wilson and Head-Prince-Babolat sizing. The photo is discarded right after processing and never uploaded.
features.item2Body: Enter palm length and ring finger length to get a recommended size and a wrap-driven size shift.
features.item3Body: Log multiple rackets with specs and notes. Stored locally in SQLite, backup whenever you want.
features.item4Body: Default restring cycles per material (polyester, multifilament, natural gut). Local notifications when a job is due.
features.item5Body: Convert DT ⇄ RT ⇄ lbs ⇄ kg in one place, then tap once to write the result straight into a restring record.

privacyStrip.heading: Your photos stay on your phone.
privacyStrip.body: AI measurement runs entirely on-device. Once your photo is processed, we neither store nor upload it.

download.androidBody: Primary platform today. Minimum Android 7.0 (API 24), target API 34, about {fileSize}. No root and no Google Play Services required.
download.androidNote: Android blocks unknown sources on first install. Open Settings, Apps, Special app access, Install unknown apps, allow this source, then tap the APK again.
download.iosBody: No iOS build yet. The TestFlight invite link will be posted here when it is ready.

faq.heading: AceCrush Craft Related
faq.q1: How accurate is the AI measurement?
faq.a1: We return a recommended size plus or minus one adjacent size with a confidence hint. Geometric error between your palm plane and the A4 sheet is a known physical limit. We do not claim millimeter precision and we do not fabricate percentage numbers.
faq.q2: Do I have to use A4 paper?
faq.a2: We strongly recommend it. A4 is a reference of known size used to convert pixels into millimeters. Other sheet sizes or objects work too, as long as you know their real dimensions when taking the photo.
faq.q3: What if my photo is taken at an angle?
faq.a3: Try to shoot straight down. If the angle is off, the confidence drops to medium or low and the result may drift by one or two grip sizes. Recompute with a flatter photo in that case.
faq.q4: Can I skip the camera and measure manually?
faq.a4: Yes. The manual entry lets you type palm length and ring finger length without invoking the camera. The two flows coexist and you can switch at any time.

intro.headline: Every swing, cut and timecoded.
intro.subtext: Feed in a match video. The two-pass pipeline tracks a single right-wrist signal, cuts each swing into its own clip, and labels ready, windup, contact and follow-through with exact timecodes.

features.heading: Built for frame-level review.
features.subheading: Three things it does that scrubbing a timeline cannot.
features.item1Body: The v2.1 pipeline reads one right-wrist signal to find swing boundaries, then refines them offline. Every segment carries ready, windup, contact and follow-through phases with timecodes.
features.item2Body: Segments appear while pass 1 is still running, so you can start reviewing before the full video finishes processing.
features.item3Body: Want to see the body lines on each clip? Two passes to choose from. The **fast pass** paints the skeleton while it cuts — quick and good enough for a first review. The **polish pass** re-renders each clip afterward with a steadier person box and a smoother skeleton — slower, but the kind of cut you'd hand to a student. Both bake straight into the export, no post-processing needed.

download.desktopBody: Runs on Windows, macOS and Linux. A Python backend plus an Electron GUI, with a CLI for terminal use. The models ship inside the repo, so clone and run works offline.
download.releasesNote: GitHub will redirect you to the current latest release.

faq.heading: Swing Analysis Related
faq.q1: Does my video get uploaded anywhere?
faq.a1: No. Everything runs on your own machine. The local service binds to 127.0.0.1 only, and your video never leaves the computer.
faq.q2: How does it decide where a swing starts?
faq.a2: The v2.1 pipeline uses a single signal, your right wrist, tracked by MediaPipe pose. Pass 1 emits candidate segments while streaming, then an offline pass refines the boundaries and labels the four phases.
faq.a3: No, it runs on CPU. The RTMDet and RTMPose overlays are the heaviest step and are entirely optional, so you can switch them off for a much faster first pass.
faq.q4: Can I use it without the desktop GUI?
faq.a4: Yes. The CLI drives the exact same pipeline, and the local REST plus WebSocket service on port 8321 is open to any front end you want to build.

download.heading: Downloads
download.subheading: AceCrush Craft ships as an Android APK today. Swing Analysis runs from source while packaged desktop builds are in progress.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.section1Body: Every record you create in AceCrush Craft (grip size measurements, racket profiles, restring logs) is saved under your own Supabase account, with row-level security so only you can read your own rows. There is no separate AceCrush-side server that aggregates, profiles, or sells your data: the Supabase project IS the only place these rows live, and each user only sees their own. A local SQLite copy on your device acts as a read-through cache so the app stays usable offline.
privacy.section2Title: Sync across every device you sign in to
privacy.section2Body: Sign in with the same Supabase account on another Android device, and later on iOS and desktop, and your racket archives and restring logs show up there too. Sync is just your row being read on the new device: no central feed, no shared timeline, no public profile. Signing out on a device clears its local copy the next time the app talks to Supabase.
privacy.section3Camera: Camera (android.permission.CAMERA): used only on the AI measurement screen. Revoke in system settings to disable.
privacy.section3Notification: Notifications (android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS): used only for restring expiry reminders. Disable in system settings.
privacy.section4Body: When you take a measurement photo, the app processes it on-device (MediaPipe HandLandmarker). If your hardware cannot keep up, the photo is sent once to our server-side OpenCV plus MediaPipe pipeline. Either way, the photo is discarded immediately after the recommended grip size is computed. It is not saved to your Supabase account, not added to your photo library, and not retained on the server after processing.
privacy.section5Body: Supabase (supabase.com) provides the authentication and the per-user database behind row-level security. We do not run any extra backend on top: the Supabase project IS the storage. Open source libraries used locally: Flutter, drift, flutter_local_notifications, url_launcher, opencv_dart, MediaPipe Tasks Vision. None of these phone home.
privacy.section6Body: Policy updates ship with new app releases and are reflected both in the in-app Settings - Privacy policy screen and on this page. Questions: acecrushdev@gmail.com.
